pr_body:
Assert JSONs not as strings, but as maps, so we don't depend on the order of the fields in the JSON object. 

Fixes #82831

comments: @arteam this might be related to https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/82670. Looks like it's just a matter of response order not matching the exact order in the request. Perhaps we should just change the assertions to be order-insensitive here.
I've gone ahead and muted this in `master` since it's failed a number of times and reliably reproduces.
Muted in `8.0` as well since there were failures there as well.

The changes in  #82670 expose a pre-existing issue in the test - it inadvertently relies on iteration order of Map, which is a test bug.

Iteration order of Map depends on may factors including, but not limited to, size, capacity, resize, or in the case of Map::of a per-JVM instance salt. For example:

```
jshell> Map<String,Integer> map1 = new HashMap<>(5)
map1 ==> {}

jshell> map1.put("Bob", 1); map1.put("Alice", 1); map1.put("Fred", 1)
$2 ==> null
$3 ==> null
$4 ==> null

jshell> map1.toString()
$5 ==> "{Fred=1, Bob=1, Alice=1}"

jshell> Map<String,Integer> map2 = new HashMap<>()
map2 ==> {}

jshell> map2.put("Bob", 1); map2.put("Alice", 1); map2.put("Fred", 1)
$7 ==> null
$8 ==> null
$9 ==> null

jshell> map2.toString()
$10 ==> "{Bob=1, Alice=1, Fred=1}"
```
I've seen this test failing, I've fixed a similar error in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/commit/bc91cd031696195140abbf56fa96545962566caf. Let me fix the test.

review_comments:
Isn't the map creation in the test itself still problematic since the response is going to be in natural order but here we're still using a hashmap?

If there's no expectation on ordering here I really think the _better_ thing to do is make the test more robust and indifferent to ordering rather than have to have to use stable collections all over the place.
Good point @mark-vieira! I've reverted the change in `PutPrivilegesResponse` and amended the assertions to check the JSONs not as strings, but as maps.
